harness: Each row's example runs in this harness: `container` is the timeline's element, `items` five tasks over March 2026, each in a lane of its own (`lanes`), with `progress`; `dependencies` a finish-to-start chain; `DAY` a day in milliseconds. `before` runs before `createTimeline`, `config` goes into its configuration, `after` runs with `timeline`. Every plugin is registered first (`registerPlugin` with the Gantt chart, the resource view, export, the time tools, groups, item kinds and other languages), as a page moving from frappe-gantt would: frappe-gantt draws all of its features without asking. Register only the ones your configuration uses, and a page loads only those.

statuses.renamed: Same meaning, another name or place.
statuses.different: Possible, done another way — read the note.

rows.note: A task is an item in a lane of its own: the lanes are the chart's rows. `gantt` turns on the arrows, the progress fill and milestones; `mountTaskGrid` draws the table beside it.
Hand the timeline the next array; it redraws once.
Several at once in one call; `undefined` takes a field away.
A key given as `undefined` goes back to its default; a key left out keeps its value.
In CSS pixels. Without one, the container's own height.
Month and day names come from `Intl` for any locale; the timeline's own words from `strings` (`@temporeum/timeline-core/intl`).
Day, week, month and year are the default presets. A preset zooms the view to that span; the columns follow the zoom instead of being redrawn per mode.
The presets are buttons over the timeline.
The first view. Without a domain the view fits the tasks, with a margin.
rows.config:
gantt: { dependencies },
domain: [new Date("2026-03-01"), new Date("2026-04-03")]

rows.note: The library never reads the clock; the host passes the time.
rows.after:
const now = new Date("2026-03-16"); // Date.now() in an app
timeline.scrollTo(now);

rows.note: Not built in; one line of the host's.
The view pans without end unless `limits` bounds it.
rows.config:
gantt: { dependencies },
limits: { min: new Date("2026-01-01"), max: new Date("2026-12-31") }

rows.note: A hidden stretch is cut out of the axis; with `repeat` it is a pattern — here every weekend.
rows.config:
gantt: { dependencies },
hiddenDates: [{ start: new Date("2026-03-07T00:00:00Z"), end: new Date("2026-03-09T00:00:00Z"), repeat: "weekly" }]

rows.temporeum: decorations: [{ kind: "era", id, start, end, label }]
rows.note: A named stretch drawn behind the tasks, with its label. A one-day holiday is a day long.
rows.config:
gantt: { dependencies },
decorations: [{ kind: "era", id: "easter", start: new Date("2026-04-03"), end: new Date("2026-04-07"), label: "Easter" }]

rows.note: One function for every axis label; `tick.granularity` says what the label stands for.
Row height follows the density; `auto` picks one at which every row fits.
A label stays on the visible part of a bar the edge cuts off; one that does not fit inside its bar is shortened with an ellipsis, or given up with `labelOverflow: "drop"`.
On hover and on keyboard focus. The text is the item's; the library adds no HTML of its own.
A Temporeum timeline is read-only until `editing.enabled`; frappe-gantt is editable until `readonly`.
Per item, with editing on.
In milliseconds, from the epoch or `snapOrigin`. A grid of whole days lies on the timeline's `timeZone` midnights, all year.
rows.config:
gantt: { dependencies },
editing: { enabled: true, snapMs: DAY }

rows.note: A move moves one task. The scheduler of `@temporeum/timeline-core/schedule` says where the ones after it go — with lags, constraints and working calendars — and `setItems` puts them there.
One lane per task, with the same id, keeps one task per row.
rows.before:
const extra = { id: "docs", laneId: "docs", label: "Docs", start: new Date("2026-03-16"), end: new Date("2026-03-20") };
const allLanes = [...lanes, { id: "docs", label: "Docs" }];

rows.note: Also the item's accessible name.

rows.temporeum: item.start, item.end: Date or epoch ms
rows.note: frappe-gantt reads a date string as local midnight, and a date-only end as the end of that day. `new Date(2026, 2, 6)` is local midnight; `new Date("2026-03-06")` is UTC midnight. For an inclusive end, add a day.
Divide by 100. Drawn as the filled part of the bar.
One list for the whole chart, each with its type (`FS` by default) and lag.
rows.before:
const frappeDeps = [{ id: "test", dependencies: "build, design" }];
const fromFrappe = frappeDeps.flatMap((task) => task.dependencies.split(",").map((from) => ({ from: from.trim(), to: task.id })));

rows.note: Colours come from the theme's custom properties and the item's class.
Give the end: start plus the duration.
rows.before:
const begin = new Date("2026-03-23");
const review = { id: "review", laneId: "test", label: "Review", start: begin, end: new Date(begin.getTime() + 3 * DAY) };

rows.note: The tooltip reads it from the item, or from `data`.
rows.config:

tooltip: (item) => (item.id === "build" ? "Build the release" : null)

rows.note: A diamond at its start, with the `gantt` option.
Also fires for `Enter` on the focused item.
`item` is `null` when the pointer leaves every item.
Each carries the item, where it was, where it is now, and the reversible command. The library never saves.

timeline.on("itemMoved", ({ item, to }) => console.log(item.id, to.start, to.end));

rows.note: Fires for every change of the view, with its reason.
A drag on empty time selects a range; a click on it selects nothing.
Progress is drawn, not dragged: change it with `updateItems`.
`baseline` draws the planned span under the bar, which shows a slip; an expected-progress mark is not drawn.
Arrows are routed around the bars with right angles.
The grid follows the axis ticks and the lanes; it is styled, not switched off by an option.
The axis is one band of its own height.
No picture on the bar itself; a `template` draws sanitised HTML in its place.
